subject: [PATCH] memcg: free the private ID of a memcg that never comes online

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that backporting the patch requires an alternative solution for older kernels and is considering using CSS_RELEASED as a workaround.
reviews.raw_body:
Oh I just noticed that private_id_objcg is introduced in 7.4, so to
backport the fix to previous stable kernels, we will still need to use
CSS_RELEASED or something else there.

2026-11-23.patch_summary: This patch addresses a memory leak issue in the Linux kernel's memcg (memory cgroup) subsystem. When a memcg is created but never comes online, its private ID remains reserved and cannot be reused. The patch introduces a new check in the css_is_released function to determine if a memcg has come online or not. If it hasn't, the patch removes the private ID from the mem_cgroup_private_ids list in the mem_cgroup_css_free function. This prevents memory leaks caused by failed cgroup creation attempts and ensures that IDs are properly reused.

reviews.author: Muchun Song
reviews.summary: Reviewer Muchun Song acknowledged the patch's logic and agreed that using private_id_objcg is a good approach to track whether the reservation was published.
reviews.raw_body:
You're right. I missed that the css is visible to mem_cgroup_iter()
before ->css_online() completes. Using private_id_objcg to track whether
the reservation was published makes sense to me. Thanks Shakeel!

reviews.author: Muchun Song
reviews.summary: Reviewer agreed with the patch and acknowledged its usefulness for backporting, providing an Acked-by tag.
reviews.raw_body:
Agreed. Keeping CSS_RELEASED in the fix makes sense for backporting.

So:

Acked-by: Muchun Song (ByteDance) <muchun.song@linux.dev>
